title: Gauging the Productivity of Team Members Who Work Remotely
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece pushes back on leaders who remain suspicious of remote and hybrid team members' productivity despite the evidence favoring flexible work. It argues that broad distrust leaks out through comments and decisions, damaging morale even for team members who are working hard. Rather than surveillance, the article recommends more frequent check-ins, clearer expectations around response times, and richer face-to-face time when it happens. The takeaway is that leading remote teams well is a distinct skill leaders have had to develop, not just a matter of trusting people more.
points: Some leaders remain suspicious of remote work despite strong evidence it boosts productivity and satisfaction.

Leading remote and hybrid teams well requires a distinct, learned skill set, not just more trust.
